A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AIM with the same authors, central method, and main experiments. Text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison. V1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–C.

before.justification: V1 reports original image and video benchmark evaluations, token-merging and pruning ablations, and accuracy-efficiency results in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: V2 retains these original evaluations and adds baseline results, computational-overhead measurements, and experiments in Appendix Tables A–E.

M1.justification: Both versions use within-frame similarity-based merging before the LLM, PageRank-based visual-token pruning, preserved text tokens, and the same piecewise scheduler. V2 clarifies encoder placement and corrects a token-count expression, without establishing a different implemented procedure.

E1.justification: The same six video benchmarks and seven image benchmarks remain in use. Appendix experiments reuse this coverage; the additional base model, frame counts, and merging configurations change experimental settings rather than datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 add VTW and PDrop to the evaluated pruning baselines, with PDrop omitted from the lowest-budget image comparison. They remove VILA, PLLaVA, LLaVA-N-Video, IXC-2.5, BLIP-2, and InstructBLIP comparison rows. Appendix B additionally compares pruning against FlashAttention.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct evaluation with reduced MAX_PIXELS, controlled 128-frame comparisons, temporal-versus-spatial merging experiments, and a merging-only/FlashAttention/pruning comparison. Appendix C adds another computation-budget configuration. The original main-experiment splits, metrics, and stated defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v2 tests whether dense frames alone explain improvements, directly compares temporal and spatial merging, and examines dependence on the base model (Tables A–C). Table 7 quantifies merging/pruning overhead, while Table D compares pruning with FlashAttention. These substantially expand the evidence examining design choices and efficiency.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for its experiments. The additional results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial baseline, overhead, and appendix results, including Qwen2-VL+AIM scoring 52.8 on VideoMME in Table C, while removing several reference-model result rows. Main AIM scores are retained. FastV's higher-budget MMB score changes from 72.7 to 72.1 in Table 3; Table 1's relative FLOP/prefill percentages change from 62.4%/63.3% to 69.5%/69.2%, consistent with comparison against FastV.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the next-layer token-count expression from N_0 r^l to N^1 r^l, using the post-merging count instead of the original count. This is a limited mathematical correction. The PageRank equation, piecewise scheduler, and absence of formal proofs are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free adaptive inference, image/video applicability, computational savings, and improved long-video performance. The stated approximately sevenfold video FLOP reduction and +4.6 MLVU result remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B explicitly identifies incompatibility with FlashAttention because pruning requires attention values, discusses other efficiency techniques, and proposes future integration. Appendix A attributes larger Qwen2-VL performance losses to joint frame encoding and discusses LLaVA-Prumerge's incompatibility with that model. V2 also interprets the newly quantified overhead as negligible; the earlier TextVQA limitation remains.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code availability from a future promise to a statement that code is available at the same repository. Appendix A discloses a memory-driven MAX_PIXELS reduction, although its value is unspecified. Existing main-experiment hyperparameters and FLOP/prefill estimation details are retained; v2 removes the explicit statement that baseline official implementations were used.

R1.justification: V2 updates related work with VTW, DyCoke, multimodal chain-of-thought work, and adaptive inference for MLLMs, and adds references supporting the FlashAttention, sparse-attention, and quantization discussion. PDrop receives explicit positioning beyond the earlier concurrent-work citation. Some background references disappear, but AIM's central positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 condenses portions of related work, clarifies the merging explanation, revises baseline descriptions, and corrects the erroneous reference to Experiment 16 to Experiment 6. It adds acknowledgements and appendix sections while retaining the main section order and most existing prose.

P2.justification: V2 adds an overhead table and Appendix Tables A–E, substantially extending the displayed evidence. Tables 1 and 3 have revised comparison rows, while existing figures and tables are resized and repositioned with revised captions and highlighting. Figures 1–2 retain their substantive content, and the original adaptive-inference Table 7 becomes Table 8.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for AIM's efficiency and design choices through overhead accounting, controlled dense-frame and temporal-merging tests, another base model, and additional relevant pruning baselines. Its explicit FlashAttention limitation also improves the assessment of practical applicability. These address important evidential gaps in v1 and outweigh the loss of several broad reference-model comparisons, although the new Qwen2-VL pixel setting remains underspecified.
